faq.a: JPG/JPEG photos from cameras and smartphones almost always have EXIF data. PNG and WebP may have XMP metadata. HEIC files have extensive metadata. Screenshots and images from social media usually have metadata stripped.
No. All metadata parsing happens in your browser using the exifr library. Your image never leaves your device.
Use the "Remove Metadata" button to download a clean copy of your image with all metadata stripped. This is recommended before sharing photos online.

faq.q: What is GPS data in photos?
faq.a: Many smartphones embed the exact GPS coordinates where a photo was taken into the EXIF data. This can reveal your home address, workplace, or travel patterns. Always remove metadata from photos before posting them online.
